A new tip appears each week. When in doubt, verify through official channels and never share an OTP or PIN.
No real police, CBI or court will video-call to “arrest” you or ask for money to clear your name. Cut the call and report on 1930. Officials never demand payment over a call.
Messages saying your account or SIM will be blocked unless you “update KYC” via a link are scams. Banks and telecoms never ask for KYC through a link or OTP. Use only the official app.
If someone says you’ll get a refund but must install an app or approve a request, stop. Refunds never need you to enter a UPI PIN — entering a PIN sends money out, not in.
You never enter your UPI PIN to receive money. A payment “request” asking for your PIN will debit you. Approve requests only when you are the one paying.
Easy-money “like and earn” or task jobs that ask you to deposit money first are scams. Never pay to get a job, and be wary of Telegram or WhatsApp job offers.
An OTP is a key to your account. No bank, delivery agent or “executive” has a genuine reason to ask for it. If someone asks, it is a scam — end the conversation.
Messages threatening tonight’s power cut unless you call a number or pay are scams. Check your bill in the official board’s app or website, not through the message.
If you did not enter a lottery, you did not win one. Paying a “fee” or “tax” to release a prize only sends your money to the scammer. Ignore and block.
